video_title: What would it take to bring LeBron James home for one last title run & would the cost be worth it?

quotes.speaker: Jimmy Watkins
quotes.summary_phrase: The Cavaliers need to restructure their roster to become championship contenders
quotes.excerpt: the Cleveland Cavaliers have now gotten out of the 2026 NBA draft and have to look to what is plausible
quotes.quote: We mentioned on a recent podcast how the summer and the off-season is just beginning as the Cleveland Cavaliers have now gotten out of the 2026 NBA draft and have to look to what is plausible, what is possible to restructure this roster, to reconstruct this roster to potentially be a championship contender. Because as we have said on this podcast, this Cavs team is not currently a contender and the Eastern Conference is only getting stronger.

quotes.speaker: Jimmy Watkins
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden holds significant power over the Cavaliers' off-season roster construction
quotes.excerpt: There is one player that holds a lot of power over this Cleveland Cavaliers organization and the structuring
quotes.quote: There is one player that holds a lot of power over this Cleveland Cavaliers organization and the structuring behind what they can do this off-season and that is James Harden. We understand he can opt in or opt out of his player option, which would alleviate some pressure from the Cavs when it comes to them being in the second apron, if he signed a team-friendly deal rather than opting into his 40-plus million dollar contract for the 2026-2027 season.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: The Cavaliers' free agency plans are contingent on James Harden's decision
quotes.excerpt: The Cavs can't proceed with any other kind of business at this point anyway in terms of free agency
quotes.quote: Timing doesn't matter. As long as he does it by that day, that's all that matters. The Cavs can't proceed with any other kind of business at this point anyway in terms of free agency, doesn't matter. The Cavs wanted to get out of the first round and avoid giving a rookie a fully guaranteed contract. That was always part of the plan. It has nothing to do with James Harden. These things are going to happen when they happen. There are deadlines for a reason and oftentimes people push it to the deadline. And as long as he does it by the deadline, that's all that matters.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: It is beneficial for the Cavaliers to retain James Harden
quotes.excerpt: It is beneficial for the Cavs to have James Harden. And if they went back on their word
quotes.quote: It is beneficial for the Cavs to have James Harden. And if they went back on their word, and I can't imagine them doing that, I can't see them doing that. They have spent years trying to build this reputation of, hey, we're really, really friendly to players. This is a place where you can want to be. We'll take care of you, we'll protect you, all that kind of stuff. But let's say if they had some kind of inkling of, do we have second thoughts on this? Are we doubting this a little bit? It's not like all of a sudden they get that money freed up and it's like, hey, we can be big spenders in free agency. Or, hey, we can go replace James Harden with a James Harden-caliber player with the kind of savings that we get. Nope, doesn't work that way.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: The Cavaliers' playoff record is not due to a lack of a reliable third big
quotes.excerpt: Are they 19 and 23 in the playoffs because they don't have a more reliable third big, really?
quotes.quote: Are they 19 and 23 in the playoffs because they don't have a more reliable third big, really? I mean, if we're talking about the list of issues with this basketball team, to me anyway, if we're talking about the list of issues with this basketball team, a reliable third big is so far down that list. And it just, I don't think it reflects on what their post-season record is. I think they have a bunch of different things with this roster that don't make a lot of sense. There's a lot of roster imbalance. But I don't think that if the Cavs would have had a more reliable third big, that they would have been more competitive against the Knicks or they would have won that series against the Knicks.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: The Cavaliers do not see the value in investing in a third big
quotes.excerpt: I think the short answer is they just don't see the value in it.
quotes.quote: I think the short answer is they just don't see the value in it. I think every decision that the Cavs make, they have to justify by saying, all right, how much are we paying this guy? And what is the value that we're getting out of this particular player on our roster? And if they feel like the value matches the contract, at least in a roundabout way, then it's easier to justify that. But they're looking at it and they're saying, how much do we have committed to Evan Mobley and Jared Allen at this point? Do we really need to invest more money in that position group? So, I don't think they see the value in a third big. In fact, like, I think they feel like what they need out of their third big can be had with Thomas Bryant-type signings or Tristan Thompson-type signings, that they don't have to spend a lot on that position or that spot on the roster, because they don't ask for that guy to do very much.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: The Cavaliers cannot afford to add another expensive big man
quotes.excerpt: The Cavs just can't afford to pay Jared Allen 30 million dollars, Evan Mobley 50 million dollars
quotes.quote: The Cavs just can't afford to pay Jared Allen 30 million dollars, Evan Mobley 50 million dollars and then another center to play 18 minutes a game during the regular season and maybe play in the post-season, maybe not play in the post-season. They can't afford to pay another one 15 to 20 million dollars. Jimmy, to your point about the Cavs needing Dean Wade or their necessity for Dean Wade's positional size, his defensive capability, his ability to play the wing and small forward and basically being the only true size wing that they have on the roster currently, there is another player out there, a 6'9" kid from Akron, who the Cavs could pursue, should they believe that he could be another helpful piece to alleviate some of the pressures on Dean Wade.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' potential return to Cleveland is a complex possibility
quotes.excerpt: It's up to the Lakers. Really is. How much are the Lakers willing to offer LeBron?
quotes.quote: It's up to the Lakers. Really is. How much are the Lakers willing to offer LeBron? How do they treat him during these negotiations? How much do they show that they value him? Because if they treat him poorly, if they turn their back on him, if they don't offer him the kind of contract that he ultimately would want, he feels like he deserves, then he's going to look elsewhere. He's going to look at Golden State. He's going to look at Cleveland. He might look at Miami. He might look at Detroit. I don't know. There's a bunch of different places that he would probably look. The Cavs are always a possibility for LeBron. Number one, technically the second best team in the Eastern Conference, however we view them coming into the season, maybe a little bit different, but they were the team that got to the conference finals against the New York Knicks. So technically they were the second best team in the Eastern Conference.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James values legacy and narrative in his career decisions
quotes.excerpt: LeBron is very aware of everything. He speaks of the importance of legacy, narratives, pride
quotes.quote: LeBron is very aware of everything. He speaks of the importance of legacy, narratives, pride, all of that kind of stuff. There is no better story for LeBron James than to end his career in Cleveland where it all started and maybe possibly deliver this franchise another championship. So that is always going to be there. And then if there are enough basketball reasons and there's enough financial motivation, then I definitely think LeBron would consider it. I would not rule out Cleveland.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James is still an elite player worthy of a significant contract
quotes.excerpt: LeBron is still a good player that is probably all-NBA caliber. Those guys don't make 10 million dollars.
quotes.quote: LeBron is still a good player that is probably all-NBA caliber. Those guys don't make 10 million dollars. Those guys don't make 15 million dollars. You know what I'm saying? And LeBron has spent his entire career fighting for player empowerment, fighting for bigger contracts, and he's just not going to take pennies. He's not going to have it. He understands that he's not getting the max, but can he get something respectable enough from one of these other teams, one of these other suitors, Golden State, Cleveland, anybody that you want to throw out there?

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' 2014 return to Cleveland was a unique, transformative moment
quotes.excerpt: Back in 2014 it was cancel everything that we had planned. Oh, we were talking to Gordon Hayward
quotes.quote: Back in 2014 it was cancel everything that we had planned. Oh, we were talking to Gordon Hayward, sorry man, LeBron might come. Nope, later. Oh, we have to give up this in order to get underneath the set, okay, fine, no problem. You just did whatever because LeBron was the most dominant force in the NBA and the minute that he came to your organization, you had a chance to compete for a championship. Now, LeBron's not the same guy in saying that. If he makes it known that he likes Cleveland, he likes the situation, he wants to be here, you at least as an organization have to consider, okay, what would it take?

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: The Cavaliers would need to make significant roster moves to acquire LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: It wouldn't just be Jared Allen sign and trade. It wouldn't. It would be you can't resign Dean Wade
quotes.quote: It wouldn't just be Jared Allen sign and trade. It wouldn't. It would be you can't resign Dean Wade, maybe that's fine with people. It would probably be you got to trade Max Strus, you got to salary dump Dennis Schroder somewhere. You've got to make a series of salary cap moves to get to a certain point where you can go ahead with a sign and trade and give LeBron the kind of money that would make him happy, that would make him want to be here, and quite frankly, that he would deserve based on what you're paying everybody else on this roster. So it is very, very complicated, but you're right, Ethan, never say never.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown's performance in the playoffs proves his value as a second star
quotes.excerpt: Jaylen Brown just scored 29 a game, grabbed seven rebounds, had five assists. He just had the best
quotes.quote: Jaylen Brown just scored 29 a game, grabbed seven rebounds, had five assists. He just had the best year of his career. He was sixth in MVP voting. He was second team All-NBA for the second time. He's been a Finals MVP. I've seen Jaylen Brown help a team win a championship. No hypothetical about it. I've seen it. I've seen it.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James is not going to the Warriors or Pistons
quotes.excerpt: LeBron's not going anywhere and getting the max. Not at this stage of his career.
quotes.quote: LeBron's not going anywhere and getting the max. Not at this stage of his career. He's not getting it from the Lakers, he's not getting it from the Pistons, he's not going to get it from the Cavs obviously. But is it a financial number that is respectable enough that he won't thumb his nose at? And it's not about him making a bunch of money, he's made a bunch of money. It's about contract represents status. Contract represents who you are as a player, what you've accomplished, and it's a reward for that and it's a recognition of that.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James remains an elite, All-NBA caliber player
quotes.excerpt: LeBron is still, you know, he's not the best player in the NBA, he's not a top five player
quotes.quote: LeBron is still, you know, he's not the best player in the NBA, he's not a top five player in the NBA, but he's still a good player that is probably all-NBA caliber. Those guys don't make 10 million dollars. Those guys don't make 15 million dollars. You know what I'm saying? And LeBron has spent his entire career fighting for player empowerment, fighting for bigger contracts, and he's just not going to take pennies. He's not going to have it.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: The Cavaliers should consider acquiring LeBron James if he shows interest
quotes.excerpt: If LeBron makes it known that he likes Cleveland, he likes the situation, he wants to be here
quotes.quote: If LeBron makes it known that he likes Cleveland, he likes the situation, he wants to be here, you at least as an organization have to consider, okay, what would it take? And then you ultimately make the decision of what we would have left over, all the moves that we would have to make. Is it worth it for us to do? It's not bow down to LeBron and beg him to come back to Cleveland like it was in 2014. Save us, please, save us. That's what it was like in 2014. It's not that in this kind of situation. It would be a real discussion within the organization.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Acquiring LeBron James would require significant roster re-configuration
quotes.excerpt: It wouldn't just be Jared Allen sign and trade. It wouldn't. It would be you got to trade Max Strus
quotes.quote: It wouldn't just be Jared Allen sign and trade. It wouldn't. It would be you got to trade Max Strus, you got to salary dump Dennis Schroder somewhere. You've got to make a series of salary cap moves to get to a certain point where you can go ahead with a sign and trade and give LeBron the kind of money that would make him happy, that would make him want to be here, and quite frankly, that he would deserve based on what you're paying everybody else on this roster.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Mobley is a valuable but offensively limited player
quotes.excerpt: Everything about Evan Mobley is a projection. Everything about Evan Mobley is what he could become.
quotes.quote: Everything about Evan Mobley is a projection. Everything about Evan Mobley is what he could become. To this point, we have five years of evidence that say, yes, he has been a winning player, yes, he has been an impactful player, yes, he has been an effective player. But we have five years of evidence that say that his game, his development is not to the same level that you need it to be to compete for a championship. That's the difference. We're not talking about beating Toronto in round one, we're not talking about beating the Pistons. We're talking about competing for a championship. Is Evan Mobley ready to help you do that? And it doesn't feel like to me his game is ready to help the Cavs do that.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James is an elite defensive player and a proven champion
quotes.excerpt: He's already a unicorn on defense, we can admit that. We know that. Everybody will admit that.
quotes.quote: He's already a unicorn on defense, we can admit that. We know that. Everybody will admit that. He is a top five player in terms of nightly impact on the defensive end of the floor. He is a unicorn at that end of the floor. But he is still an offensively limited player. He is still somebody who has a lot to prove at that end of the floor when it comes to being an offensive focal point, when it comes to being a number one option or a number two or a number three option on the offensive end.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: The Cavaliers should explore acquiring elite players to improve their roster
quotes.excerpt: You can't give up Jared Allen, Jaylen Tyson, Malik Thomas, and like Tyrese Proctor and expect to get Jaylen Brown.
quotes.quote: You can't give up Jared Allen, Jaylen Tyson, Malik Thomas, and like Tyrese Proctor and expect to get Jaylen Brown. No, it's not going to happen that way. If you want Jaylen Brown, it's going to have to be Evan. And yes, that's hard. And yes, that's a risk. Everybody will admit that's a risk. But think about what you're getting back. And think about the talent that you're getting back. Evan Mobley may never be as good as Jaylen Brown. In fact, we got a lot of evidence that says he won't be as good as Jaylen Brown. Evan Mobley was never going to be as good as Jaylen Brown. Probably never going to be good as Jaylen Brown. That's what you're getting back. And you're a team that just invested in James Harden. You're a team that's probably going to invest in Donovan Mitchell. You know what I'm saying? It's now. This is your championship window.
